on:
  github:
    pull_request:
      # No base-branch `if:` filter -- matches .rwx/tests.yml's pull_request
      # trigger (whose GHA source declared `pull_request: {}` with no
      # branches filter), so this gate posts on every PR, including the
      # Trunk merge queue's temporary trunk-merge/* PRs, which arrive as
      # ordinary pull_request events (same mechanism gtm-sdk's queue relies
      # on; its configs narrow with base-branch == 'main', the unfiltered
      # trigger here is broader, not narrower).
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: pull_request
        # Same raw-webhook field gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml uses
        # (event.github.pull_request.pull_request.base.sha, confirmed on real
        # runs there 2026-09-26): PR-mode lint must diff against the PR's
        # exact base commit, not the moving tip of main -- the tip would
        # silently widen or narrow the lint scope whenever main has moved
        # since the PR branched.
        base-sha: ${{ event.github.pull_request.pull_request.base.sha }}
    push:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: push
        base-sha: ""
      if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
  cli:
    # Manual `rwx run` dispatch to validate the full-repo push path.
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
      event-type: push
      base-sha: ""

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: ${{ init.repository }}
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      # Full depth + preserved .git: the trunk-check task below resolves the
      # PR's base commit (git cat-file + fetch + merge-base) and diffs against it via
      # `trunk check --upstream` -- both need real git history, not a
      # shallow snapshot (same reason gtm-sdk's trunk-check code task sets
      # these flags, unlike this repo's tests.yml clone, which nothing
      # history-dependent consumes). Public repo, so no github-token is
      # needed.
      fetch-full-depth: true
      preserve-git-dir: true

  # Same checksum-pinned installer as .rwx/tests.yml's uv-install task, same
  # rationale there: the astral.sh script at a versioned URL is stable for
  # that version, and pinning the bytes makes an altered or compromised
  # script fail closed instead of executing. Version matches tests.yml's
  # (validated against uv sync --locked + the full pytest suite).
  - key: uv-install
    use: [code]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # pyright and pyrefly resolve the project's dependencies through .venv
  # (the pyright override in .trunk/trunk.yaml points at
  # ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python), so the lint gate needs the same uv sync
  # the test pipeline runs. Without it pyright fails red with confusing
  # Unknown-type findings (see the comment on that override). Exports mirror
  # tests.yml's deps task so downstream `trunk run` inherits them.
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_LOCKED: "1"
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      uv sync
      echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      echo "$PWD/.venv" > "$RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV"
      echo "1" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_LOCKED"
      echo "3.13" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_PYTHON"

  # Ports gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml trunk-check-pr task, adapted for a
  # public repo: no github-token and no GIT_ASKPASS base fetch are needed --
  # the full-depth clone already contains the PR's base commit (the head
  # descends from it), so presence is verified with git cat-file instead of
  # re-fetching. Fork PRs get full lint coverage here (unlike gtm-sdk's
  # Bazel gate, which skips them for secret safety) because this task uses
  # no secrets. Incremental mode against the exact base commit keeps the
  # required PR status diff-scoped -- a PR only lints its own changes --
  # while the push/cli trunk-check-full task below lints the whole tree.
  # The launcher is checksum-pinned (same rationale as uv-install):
  # trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only -- no versioned URL exists -- so
  # the bytes are pinned and any upstream change fails closed instead of
  # executing. gtm-sdk pins an older launcher checksum for the same reason;
  # this pin is the live bytes as of 2026-10-15 (smoke-tested: resolves to
  # the cli.version pin, 1.25.0). Re-pin deliberately, never opportunistically.
  # If this task fails with a checksum mismatch, the launcher rolled upstream:
  # re-download, re-hash, and re-pin here. Failing closed is the design -- an
  # unpinned launcher would execute whatever upstream serves -- but it reddens
  # a required status until re-pinned, so treat it as urgent.
  # `--ci` and `< /dev/null` are required, not cosmetic: without them trunk
  # can hang on an interactive prompt with no TTY/stdin (observed on gtm-sdk:
  # 2.5+ minutes of repeated cursor-clear escapes, no progress).
  # Gated on event-type: push and cli runs take trunk-check-full instead.
  - key: trunk-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" /usr/local/bin/trunk 2>/dev/null; then
        mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
        install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" "$HOME/.local/bin/trunk"
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"

  # Tool cache. RWX caches a task by its command, env, the filesystem its
  # `use` dependencies produce and its own filtered files, and carries the
  # task's filesystem (including ~/.cache/trunk) to downstream tasks. A
  # `filter` scopes only the task that defines it: downstream `use:`rs do
  # NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file
  # (rwx.com/docs/filtering-files, "Sharing filters across tasks") -- so
  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter, and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config's keys its own cache on .trunk/
  # alone, freezing the $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes for downstream keys
  # (outside-workspace files are always keyed, never filtered);
  # trunk-tools' scopes its key to .trunk/ plus the pinned launcher binary
  # trunk-install writes. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin in trunk.yaml
  # is downloaded once and reused until a pin (or other trunk.yaml edit)
  # changes; keep the two filter lists in lockstep. The seed repo is a
  # scratch git repo so `trunk install` needs nothing else from the commit;
  # the check tasks then find the tools already installed.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: [code]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
----
# This file controls the behavior of Trunk: https://docs.trunk.io/cli # To learn more about the format of this file, see https://docs.trunk.io/reference/trunk-yaml
version: 0.1
cli:
  version: 1.25.0

# Trunk provides extensibility via plugins. (https://docs.trunk.io/plugins)
plugins:
  sources:
    - id: trunk
      ref: v1.11.0
      uri: https://github.com/trunk-io/plugins

    - id: oss-linter-trunk
      ref: v0.2026.04.14.00.00

    - id: add-trailing-comma-plugin
      ref: v0.1.0
      uri: https://github.com/elviskahoro/oss-linter-trunk-add-trailing-comma

    - id: pyrefly-plugin
      ref: v0.2.0
      uri: https://github.com/elviskahoro/oss-linter-trunk-pyrefly

    - id: tach-plugin
      ref: v0.1.0
      uri: https://github.com/elviskahoro/oss-linter-trunk-tach

# actionlint switched from upstream rhysd/actionlint to the actively maintained
# fork kjanat/actionlint (forked from upstream v1.7.12, independent releases from
# v1.8.0, CLI-compatible). Trunk's plugin catalog still pins the rhysd download
# URL, so override it here until the catalog carries the fork. Asset naming and
# the -format JSON output the plugin's `lint` command relies on are unchanged.
downloads:
  - name: actionlint
    downloads:
      - os:
          linux: linux
          macos: darwin
        cpu:
          x86_64: amd64
          arm_64: arm64
        url: https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint/releases/download/v${version}/actionlint_${version}_${os}_${cpu}.tar.gz
      - os: windows
        cpu:
          x86_64: amd64
          arm_64: arm64
        url: https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint/releases/download/v${version}/actionlint_${version}_windows_${cpu}.zip

# This is the section where you manage your linters. (https://docs.trunk.io/check/configuration)
lint:
  definitions:
    - name: ruff
      commands:
        - name: format
          enabled: true
        - name: lint
          enabled: true
    # The plugin's default command checks module boundaries. Tach's external
    # dependency audit is separate, so include it in the same Trunk gate.
    #
    # No `external` command here on purpose. Trunk executes batch lint
    # commands from a sandboxed tmp dir that contains only the diff's files
    # plus direct configs, and `tach check-external` decides "used" by
    # scanning the imports visible from its cwd -- the diff, not the tree.
    # Every runtime dependency whose import sites sit outside the diff was
    # reported "not used": #108's own PR run flagged all four (httpx, pydantic,
    # pydantic_settings, typer), and any single-file Python PR trips it the
    # same way, which would reject every queue entry once the merge queue
    # gates on this pipeline. There is no way to point it at the real
    # workspace from a lint command (Trunk does binary lookup, not a shell,
    # so `cd ${workspace} && ...` dies with "Unable to find binary in PATH:
    # cd"; tach has no --root flag), so the audit lives in .rwx/lint.yml's
    # tach-external task, which runs against the full checkout and is
    # required by the same queue.
    - name: tach
      commands:
        - name: lint
          run: tach check --dependencies --interfaces --exact
    # Trunk runs linters from a sandboxed tmp dir with `env -i`, so pyright's
    # usual environment discovery (PATH lookup) lands on Trunk's own node
    # runtime, which has none of the project's dependencies. That made pyright
    # silently check the whole SDK against Unknown types (reportMissingImports
    # is "none" in the config, so nothing flagged). Point it at the project
    # venv, the same way the pyrefly plugin does for pyrefly.
    #
    # This overrides the plugin's whole pyright invocation, so re-check this
    # command against the plugin definition whenever trunk.yaml bumps plugin
    # versions. If `.venv` is missing the check fails red with confusing
    # Unknown-type findings (pyright warns about the bad --pythonpath but
    # still runs), so `uv sync` before the first check — see AGENTS.md.
    - name: pyright
      commands:
        - name: lint
          run: pyright --pythonpath ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python --outputjson ${target}

    # Trunk runs linters from a sandboxed tmp dir, so pyrefly's usual environment
    # discovery (interpreter resolution via PATH lookup) lands in Trunk's sandbox,
    # not the project workspace. The pyrefly plugin (oss-linter-trunk-pyrefly v0.2.0)
    # claims to pass --python-interpreter-path ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python and
    # --search-path ${workspace} automatically, but this fails in environments where
    # .venv/bin/python is a symlink to /usr/local/bin/python3 (typical in cloud
    # sandboxes), because pyrefly's interpreter-resolver follows the symlink target,
    # landing outside the venv's site-packages. See #120.
    #
    # This overrides the plugin's whole pyrefly invocation to explicitly pass the
    # workspace venv paths, matching the pattern used for pyright above. Re-check
    # this command against the plugin definition whenever trunk.yaml bumps plugin
    # versions.
    - name: pyrefly
      commands:
        - name: lint
          run: pyrefly check --python-interpreter-path ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python --search-path ${workspace} --output-format=min-text --summary=none ${target}

    # Vale is scoped exclusively to docs/** via a custom file type -- there is
    # no first-class "restrict this linter to a directory" field on `enabled`
    # entries, and `regexes` (unlike `extensions`) match the full path from
    # the repo root, so markdown outside docs/ (README.md, CHANGELOG.md) is
    # never picked up. Dormant until a docs/ tree and .vale.ini exist here;
    # gtm-sdk scopes its vale the same way.
version: 2
updates:
  # Bumps the SHA-pinned `uses:` refs. Renovate manages the Dagger module's
  # paired SemVer tag and immutable commit SHA in publish.yml (`.rwx/`).
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions

      interval: weekly
    # Wait 7 days after a release before proposing an update, so freshly
    # published -- possibly malicious or unstable -- action tags are not
    # picked up immediately. Dependabot's implicit default is 3 days.
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7

model = "fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash"

  hand-editing them. Fixes belong in the generator, and codegen.py --check

  per-file ignores in ruff.toml; do not flag it and do not suggest per-line

<!-- Canonical source: flox-conductor-sandbox prompts/conductor/create-pr.md.
     Installed into a repo's .conductor settings [prompts].create_pr by
     scripts/install-conductor-prompts.py — do not hand-edit the TOML copy.
     Upstream history: gtm-sdk prompts/conductor/create-pr.md (incl. #921).
     Repo-specific references (Linear, design/ artifacts,
     roborev) follow the cross-repo conventions — where a repo's own

# Creating Pull Requests

## The principle: why over what

A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.

Concretely:

- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.

A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Pre-flight checks

Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:

```bash
git status                                          # working tree clean?
git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
```

Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:

- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.

Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.

### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"

A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:

**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):

1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
4. Save the URL for the Links section.

Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.

# Dependabot keeps the CI/CD plumbing honest. Two update streams run weekly:
# GitHub Actions (which carries `trunk-io/trunk-action`,
# `astral-sh/setup-uv`, etc. -- all pinned by SHA) and uv dependency
# groups (which carries `reflex`, `pytest`, etc., resolved via
# `uv.lock`).
#
# Cost discipline: pinact (in trunk fmt) auto-rewrites inline action
# SHAs and version comments on `trunk fmt`. Dependabot bumps the SHA
# but does not touch `# v<x.y.z>` -- the `trunk fmt` push that
# accompanies the Dependabot PR is what finalizes the visible pin.
# `open-pull-requests-limit` caps how many weekly bumps stay open at
# any time so the merge queue is not overdriven.
version: 2

# A 7-day cooldown on any Dependabot bump protects the template's users
# from unknowingly picking up a malicious or unstable release the same
# day it lands upstream. Required by semgrep
# `dependabot-missing-cooldown` (high). Inline per-`updates:` block
# because semgrep's matcher reads each `updates:` entry in isolation
# rather than recognizing the top-level `cooldown.default-days`.
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      github-actions:
        patterns:
          - "*"
    # Pinact-tracked actions stay on their current SHA until the manual
    # `trunk fmt` runs in the next commit -- Dependabot bumps add the
    # green diff and the version stamp gets rewritten alongside them.
    labels:
      - "ci:actions"
      - "automated"

  - package-ecosystem: "uv"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "tuesday"
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 2
    groups:
      runtime:
        dependency-type: "production"
      dev-tools:
        dependency-type: "development"
    # pyrefly/pyright/tach versions MUST match `.trunk/trunk.yaml`,
    # so Dependabot is forbidden from bumping them automatically. A
    # version bump in those three needs coordinated edits to
    # pyproject.toml AND `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
    ignore:
      - dependency-name: "pyrefly"
      - dependency-name: "pyright"
      - dependency-name: "tach"
    labels:
      - "ci:deps"
      - "automated"

  # script fail closed instead of executing. Version matches tests.yml's

      echo "$PWD/.venv" > "$RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV"
      echo "1" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_LOCKED"
      echo "3.13" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_PYTHON"

  # required PR status diff-scoped -- a PR only lints its own changes --

  # The launcher is checksum-pinned (same rationale as uv-install):
  # trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only -- no versioned URL exists -- so
  # the bytes are pinned and any upstream change fails closed instead of
  # executing. gtm-sdk pins an older launcher checksum for the same reason;

  # unpinned launcher would execute whatever upstream serves -- but it reddens
  # a required status until re-pinned, so treat it as urgent.

  # 2.5+ minutes of repeated cursor-clear escapes, no progress).

  - key: trunk-install

        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" /usr/local/bin/trunk 2>/dev/null; then

        install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" "$HOME/.local/bin/trunk"

      fi

  # `use` dependencies produce and its own filtered files, and carries the
  # task's filesystem (including ~/.cache/trunk) to downstream tasks. A
  # `filter` scopes only the task that defines it: downstream `use:`rs do
  # NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file

  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter, and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config's keys its own cache on .trunk/
  # alone, freezing the $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes for downstream keys
  # (outside-workspace files are always keyed, never filtered);
  # trunk-tools' scopes its key to .trunk/ plus the pinned launcher binary
  # trunk-install writes. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin in trunk.yaml
  # is downloaded once and reused until a pin (or other trunk.yaml edit)
  # changes; keep the two filter lists in lockstep. The seed repo is a
  # scratch git repo so `trunk install` needs nothing else from the commit;
  # the check tasks then find the tools already installed.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: [code]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml

# Creating Pull Requests

## The principle: why over what

A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.

Concretely:

- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.

A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Pre-flight checks

Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:

```bash
git status                                          # working tree clean?
git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
```

Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:

- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.

Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.

### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"

A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:

**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):

1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
4. Save the URL for the Links section.

Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.

**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):

1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.

**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:

```bash
ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
```

- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.

**Git history**:

- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.

**Current conversation**:

- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.

If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.

# Dependabot keeps the CI/CD plumbing honest. Two update streams run weekly:
# GitHub Actions (which carries `trunk-io/trunk-action`,
# `astral-sh/setup-uv`, etc. -- all pinned by SHA) and uv dependency
# groups (which carries `reflex`, `pytest`, etc., resolved via
# `uv.lock`).
#
# Cost discipline: pinact (in trunk fmt) auto-rewrites inline action
# SHAs and version comments on `trunk fmt`. Dependabot bumps the SHA
# but does not touch `# v<x.y.z>` -- the `trunk fmt` push that
# accompanies the Dependabot PR is what finalizes the visible pin.
# `open-pull-requests-limit` caps how many weekly bumps stay open at
# any time so the merge queue is not overdriven.
version: 2

# A 7-day cooldown on any Dependabot bump protects the template's users
# from unknowingly picking up a malicious or unstable release the same
# day it lands upstream. Required by semgrep
# `dependabot-missing-cooldown` (high). Inline per-`updates:` block
# because semgrep's matcher reads each `updates:` entry in isolation
# rather than recognizing the top-level `cooldown.default-days`.
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      github-actions:
        patterns:
          - "*"
    # Pinact-tracked actions stay on their current SHA until the manual
    # `trunk fmt` runs in the next commit -- Dependabot bumps add the
    # green diff and the version stamp gets rewritten alongside them.
    labels:
      - "ci:actions"
      - "automated"

  - package-ecosystem: "uv"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "tuesday"
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 2
    groups:
      runtime:
        dependency-type: "production"
      dev-tools:
        dependency-type: "development"
    # pyrefly/pyright/tach versions MUST match `.trunk/trunk.yaml`,
    # so Dependabot is forbidden from bumping them automatically. A
    # version bump in those three needs coordinated edits to
    # pyproject.toml AND `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
    ignore:
      - dependency-name: "pyrefly"
      - dependency-name: "pyright"
      - dependency-name: "tach"
    labels:
      - "ci:deps"
      - "automated"

# Takeaways from sdk-python-linear for the Reflex starter

## Context
Scanned elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear (typed Linear SDK, same toolchain family: uv, Trunk, ruff/pyright/pyrefly/tach, RWX CI). The starter already shares most of it. Below are the gaps worth porting, ranked. Another agent covers a different repo, so these stay scoped to this one.

## Recommended changes (highest value first)

1. **uv dependency cooldown** — `pyproject.toml`: add `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days"`. Starter already has a 7-day Dependabot cooldown; this extends it to `uv lock`/`uv sync` itself.
2. **Checksum-pinned installers in RWX** — in `.rwx/*.yml` replace unpinned uv/trunk installs with the `curl … | sha256sum -c` pattern (uv versioned URL; trunk launcher hash). Fails closed on a tampered script. Reference: `.rwx/lint.yml` `uv-install`, `trunk-install`.
3. **Cache trunk tools in RWX** — add `trunk-config` / `trunk-tools` tasks (filter on `.trunk/`) so linter downloads are reused across runs; use `--ci` and `< /dev/null` to avoid hangs. Applies to `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, `smoke-nightly.yml`.
4. **Tach external-dependency audit as its own RWX task** — add a `tach-external` task running `uv run tach check-external` on the full checkout (the Trunk batch sandbox can't do it; the sdk repo documents why). Starter's tach.toml already sets `unused_external_dependencies = "error"`, so this makes it actually enforced.
5. **pytest hygiene** — `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`: register markers (e.g. `network`) with `addopts = "-m 'not network'"` for live/slow tests; add `pytest-asyncio` with `asyncio_mode = "auto"` if async tests grow.
6. **Drift-check pattern** — repo guards generated artifacts with `--check` scripts plus a pytest (`test_codegen_is_current.py`). Apply to the starter only if it has generated files (e.g. `reflex.lock`, `.web`); otherwise skip.
7. **Agent docs** — `AGENTS.md`: add a "Build & Test" command block, an "Architecture Overview", "Conventions & Patterns" (why per-file ruff ignores exist), non-interactive shell rules, and a "RWX CI: green ≠ worked, read logs" note. Add `.roborev.toml` `review_guidelines` encoding deliberate decisions so reviewers stop re-flagging them.
8. **Explanatory comments on pins** — sdk repo documents *why* each version/pin/override in `pyproject.toml` and `trunk.yaml`; add the same to starter's pyrefly/pyright/tach pins and the trunk overrides.
9. **Trunk Merge Queue section in AGENTS.md** (optional) — only if you use the queue for the starter; the sdk repo's rules (never `gh pr merge`, one status check, no force) are reusable verbatim.
10. **Renovate for pinned non-ecosystem refs** (optional) — regex manager pattern for SHA+tag pairs in RWX files; skip unless starter has such pins.

## Deliberately not ported
Codegen toolchain, GraphQL schema/operations, CLI (typer), Captain/flaky-test upload, Dagger publish, Beads (repo has dropped it), looser ruff config (starter's `select = ["ALL"]` is stricter — keep it).

## Verification
- `uv lock && uv sync --group dev && uv run pytest -q`
- `trunk check --all`; `uv run tach check` and `uv run tach check-external`
- `rwx lint .rwx/*.yml`; `rwx run .rwx/trunk-check.yml --wait` on the branch and read task logs

## Open question
Which items do you want? Default: 1–5, 7, 8.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )

  return { confirmed }

## Context
Scanned elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear (typed Linear SDK, same toolchain family: uv, Trunk, ruff/pyright/pyrefly/tach, RWX CI). The starter already shares most of it. Below are the gaps worth porting, ranked. Another agent covers a different repo, so these stay scoped to this one.

## Recommended changes (highest value first)

1. **uv dependency cooldown** — `pyproject.toml`: add `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days"`. Starter already has a 7-day Dependabot cooldown; this extends it to `uv lock`/`uv sync` itself.
2. **Checksum-pinned installers in RWX** — in `.rwx/*.yml` replace unpinned uv/trunk installs with the `curl … | sha256sum -c` pattern (uv versioned URL; trunk launcher hash). Fails closed on a tampered script. Reference: `.rwx/lint.yml` `uv-install`, `trunk-install`.
3. **Cache trunk tools in RWX** — add `trunk-config` / `trunk-tools` tasks (filter on `.trunk/`) so linter downloads are reused across runs; use `--ci` and `< /dev/null` to avoid hangs. Applies to `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, `smoke-nightly.yml`.
4. **Tach external-dependency audit as its own RWX task** — add a `tach-external` task running `uv run tach check-external` on the full checkout (the Trunk batch sandbox can't do it; the sdk repo documents why). Starter's tach.toml already sets `unused_external_dependencies = "error"`, so this makes it actually enforced.
5. **pytest hygiene** — `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`: register markers (e.g. `network`) with `addopts = "-m 'not network'"` for live/slow tests; add `pytest-asyncio` with `asyncio_mode = "auto"` if async tests grow.
6. **Drift-check pattern** — repo guards generated artifacts with `--check` scripts plus a pytest (`test_codegen_is_current.py`). Apply to the starter only if it has generated files (e.g. `reflex.lock`, `.web`); otherwise skip.
7. **Agent docs** — `AGENTS.md`: add a "Build & Test" command block, an "Architecture Overview", "Conventions & Patterns" (why per-file ruff ignores exist), non-interactive shell rules, and a "RWX CI: green ≠ worked, read logs" note. Add `.roborev.toml` `review_guidelines` encoding deliberate decisions so reviewers stop re-flagging them.
8. **Explanatory comments on pins** — sdk repo documents *why* each version/pin/override in `pyproject.toml` and `trunk.yaml`; add the same to starter's pyrefly/pyright/tach pins and the trunk overrides.
9. **Trunk Merge Queue section in AGENTS.md** (optional) — only if you use the queue for the starter; the sdk repo's rules (never `gh pr merge`, one status check, no force) are reusable verbatim.
10. **Renovate for pinned non-ecosystem refs** (optional) — regex manager pattern for SHA+tag pairs in RWX files; skip unless starter has such pins.

Codegen toolchain, GraphQL schema/operations, CLI (typer), Captain/flaky-test upload, Dagger publish, Beads (repo has dropped it), looser ruff config (starter's `select = ["ALL"]` is stricter — keep it).

## Verification
- `uv lock && uv sync --group dev && uv run pytest -q`
- `trunk check --all`; `uv run tach check` and `uv run tach check-external`
- `rwx lint .rwx/*.yml`; `rwx run .rwx/trunk-check.yml --wait` on the branch and read task logs

Which items do you want? Default: 1–5, 7, 8.

## Build & Test

```bash
uv sync --group dev          # install locked deps into .venv
uv run pytest -q             # smoke tests (`network`-marked tests deselected)
uv run tach check            # module boundaries
uv run tach check-external   # declared vs imported dependencies
trunk check --all            # lint (run uv sync first: pyright/pyrefly use .venv)
```

## Conventions

- Layers are `web.web` -> `web.pages.*` -> `web.components.*`, enforced by
  `tach.toml`; new modules need an explicit entry there.
- `tach check-external` is its own task in `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, not a Trunk
  linter: Trunk lints from a sandbox holding only the diff, which makes every
  dependency look unused.
- `uv` ignores packages published in the last 7 days (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer`);
  pyrefly/pyright/tach pins must match between `pyproject.toml` and
  `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- RWX: a green run is not proof a step worked. Read task logs (`rwx logs`) for
  steps that talk to third parties.
- Use non-interactive flags (`-y`, `-f`, `trunk ... --ci < /dev/null`) in
  scripted commands.

## Git workflow

28	
29	# Creating Pull Requests
30	
31	## The principle: why over what
32	
33	A PR description's job is to give the reviewer what the diff *can't*: motivation, alternatives considered, risks worth scrutinizing, and a trail back to the originating context. The diff itself is the source of truth for what changed — paraphrasing it in the description is duplicate work that rots the moment someone force-pushes.
34	
35	Concretely:
36	
37	- Lead with the **problem**, not the change.
38	- Name the **alternatives** you considered, briefly. Skip if there were no meaningful ones.
39	- Call out what reviewers should **scrutinize**, not what they should take on faith.
40	- Link the **breadcrumb trail** — Linear ticket, design spec/plan, predecessor PR.
41	- **Never** summarize the diff. The reviewer is about to read it.
42	
43	A reader who skims your description should walk away with the mental model needed to read the diff with intention.
44	
45	## Workflow
46	
47	### Step 1: Pre-flight checks
48	
49	Before drafting, run these in a single batch of parallel `Bash` calls:
50	
51	```bash
52	git status                                          # working tree clean?
53	git branch --show-current                           # current branch?
54	git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null  # is there a remote tracking ref?
55	git log @{upstream}..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null     # any unpushed commits?
56	git log main..HEAD --oneline                        # commits beyond main?
57	git diff main...HEAD --stat                         # surface area?
58	gh pr view --json url,state 2>/dev/null             # does a PR already exist?
59	gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name  # confirm base
60	```
61	
62	Stop and surface the problem to the user if any of these is true:
63	
64	- The working tree has uncommitted changes — ask the user whether to commit, stash, or abandon.
65	- The branch has no upstream / is not pushed — confirm with the user before pushing.
66	- The branch has zero commits beyond the base — there's nothing to PR.
67	- A PR already exists for this branch — use `gh pr edit` to update it, not `gh pr create`.
68	
69	Don't paper over these by force-pushing, amending, or running `git push -f`. The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) apply: destructive operations need explicit user approval.
70	
71	### Step 2: Gather context for the "Why"
72	
73	A strong Why section comes from upstream artifacts, not from the diff. Pull from these sources in parallel where possible:
74	
75	**Linear ticket** — if the branch name matches `(feature|agent)/<team>-<number>-<slug>` (e.g., `feature/ai-268-foo`, `agent/eng-1234-bar`):
76	
77	1. Extract the ticket ID with a regex like `[A-Z]+-\d+` (case-insensitive).
78	2. Read it via `mcp__linear__get_issue` with the identifier.
79	3. Lift the problem statement and acceptance criteria into the Why section — **paraphrase, don't paste**. A wall of quoted ticket text isn't a PR description.
80	4. Save the URL for the Links section.
81	
82	Skip the Linear lookup when the repo doesn't use Linear (no Linear MCP configured, no matching branch pattern) — rely on the sources below.
83	
84	**GitHub issue** — if the user linked or named a GitHub issue this session (a URL, `#NNN`, or an issue the branch was created for, e.g., `conductor/gtm-sdk-issue-608`):
85	
86	1. Note whether it's same-repo or cross-repo (a bare `#NNN` or number is same-repo; a URL or `owner/repo#NNN` names the repo explicitly — keep that `owner/repo` around for every later step). Fetch it with `gh issue view <number>` for a same-repo issue, or `gh issue view <number> --repo <owner/repo>` otherwise, to confirm it's still open and pull the problem statement into the Why section — paraphrase, don't paste.
87	2. Ask yourself (and, if unclear, the user) whether this PR **fully** resolves the issue or only partial work. Carry that determination into Step 7's Links section and Step 9.
88	3. Save the issue reference for the Links section either way.
89	
90	**Design artifacts** — scan `design/` (when the repo uses the design-artifact convention) for backlog/done files matching the branch topic:
91	
92	```bash
93	ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
94	```
95	
96	- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
97	- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
98	- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.
99	
100	**Git history**:
101	
102	- `git log main..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.
103	
104	**Current conversation**:
105	
106	- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.
107	
108	If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.
109	
110	### Step 3: Commit local changes
111	
112	If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.
113	
114	- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
115	- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject. The Step 8 draft approval is still the only user-approval gate before push.
116	- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, the user-confirmation gate, and the rebase.
117	
118	If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.

120	### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits
121

123	
124	```bash
125	git log main..HEAD --oneline
126	```
127	
128	- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
129	- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
130	- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.

135

137	
138	- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.

141

144	With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:
145	
146	```bash
147	roborev review --wait
148	```
149	
150	- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
151	- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
152	- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
153	- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
154	- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
155	- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
156	- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.
157	
158	### Step 6: Draft the title
159	
160	The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.
161	
162	Rules:
163	
164	- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
165	- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
166	- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
167	- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
168	- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
169	- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
170	- **No trailing period.**
171	- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.
172	
173	Good vs. bad title shapes:
174	
175	| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
176	| --- | --- |
177	| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
178	| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
179	| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
180	| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |
181	
182	### Step 7: Draft the description
183	
184	Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.
185	
186	```markdown
187	## Why
188	<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>
189	
190	## Trade-offs
191	<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>
192	
193	## Risks
194	<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>
195	
196	## Test plan
197	<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>
198	
199	## Links
200	- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
201	- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
202	- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
203	- Related PRs: #NNN
204	- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
205	```
206	
207	Section guidance:
208	
209	| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
210	| --- | --- | --- |
211	| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
212	| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
213	| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
214	| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
215	| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |
216	
217	### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)
218	
219	**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.
220	
221	Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.
222	
223	**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.
224	
225	Format the preview as:
226	
227	```text
228	Title: <draft title>
229	
230	Body:
231	---
232	<draft body>
233	---
234	
235	Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>
236	
237	Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
238	```
239	
240	The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.
241	
242	If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).
243	
244	### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition
245	
246	If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:
247	
248	- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
249	- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
250	- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
251	- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
252	- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.
253	
254	### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)
255	
256	**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.
257	
258	This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.
259	
260	```bash
261	git fetch origin
262	git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
263	```
264	
265	- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
266	- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
267	- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.
268	
269	### Step 11: Push the branch
270	
271	Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.
272	
273	```bash
274	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
275	```
276	
277	Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.
278	
279	### Step 12: Create the PR
280	
281	**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:
282	
283	```bash
284	grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
285	```
286	
287	`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.
288	
289	If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.
290	
291	To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:
292	
293	```bash
294	PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
295	## Why
296	... (real newlines, not \n)
297	EOF
298	)"
299	
300	for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
301	  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
302	    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
303	    exit 1
304	  }
305	done
306	
307	gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
308	```
309	
310	Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.
311	
312	### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it
313	
314	Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.
315	
316	```bash
317	gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
318	gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
319	```
320	
321	- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
322	- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
323	- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.
324	
325	### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass
326	
327	Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:
328	
329	```bash
330	gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
331	```
332	
333	- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
334	- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
335	- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.
336	
337	## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels
338	
339	`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:
340	
341	| Flag | When |
342	| --- | --- |
343	| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
344	| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
345	| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
346	| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
347	| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |
348	
349	## Anti-patterns
350	
351	These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.
352	
353	### Don't summarize the diff
354	
355	```markdown
356	## Summary
357	- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
358	- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
359	- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
360	```
361	
362	The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.
363	
364	### Don't write empty sections
365	
366	```markdown
367	## Risks
368	None.
369	
370	## Test plan
371	Tested locally.
372	```
373	
374	"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.
375	
376	### Don't add AI attribution
377	
378	The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
379	**Never** emit:
380	
381	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
382	- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
383	- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer
384	
385	The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.
386	
387	### Don't restate the title
388	
389	If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.
390	
391	### Don't pad with boilerplate
392	
393	- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
394	- "As discussed offline, ..."
395	- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."
396	
397	If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.
398	
399	### Don't paste test output
400	
401	The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.
402	
403	### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming
404	
405	GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.
406	
407	### Don't autopilot the PR submission
408	
409	Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.
410

412	
413	### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only
414	
415	**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`
416	
417	**Body:**
418	
419	```markdown
420	## Why
421	The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).
422	
423	## Links
424	- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
425	```
426	
427	(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)
428	
429	### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links
430	
431	**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`
432	
433	**Body:**
434	
435	```markdown
436	## Why
437	Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.
438	
439	Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.
440	
441	## Trade-offs
442	Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.
443	
444	## Risks
445	Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.
446	
447	## Links
448	- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
449	- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
450	```
451	
452	### Example 3: Bad → Good
453	
454	**Bad:**
455	
456	```markdown
457	## Summary
458	- Added retry decorator
459	- Updated 5 Attio call sites
460	- Removed duplicate retry code
461	- Added tests
462	
463	## Test plan
464	- [x] Ran tests
465	- [x] Tested locally
466	
467	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
468	```
469	
470	What's wrong: the Summary paraphrases the diff, the Test plan has no reasoning, the AI footer is forbidden, and there's no motivation a reviewer can use to evaluate the change.
471	
472	**Good:** see Example 2.

474	## Failure modes and recovery
475	
476	| What happened | What to do |
477	| --- | --- |
478	| Linear MCP unavailable or ticket not found | Continue without the Linear context. Note in Links: "Linear ticket: AI-NNN (MCP unavailable at draft time)" and let the user fill in. |
479	| Branch doesn't match a Linear pattern | Skip the Linear lookup. Rely on design artifacts and conversation. |
480	| No design artifact, no ticket, no clear Why from the conversation | Stop. Ask the user: "I can't establish a specific Why for this PR from the available context. Can you summarize the motivation in 1-2 sentences?" |
481	| `gh pr create` fails (auth, network, no remote) | Surface the error to the user. Don't retry without diagnosing. |
482	| User rejects the draft | Take their feedback and rewrite. Don't argue. |
483	| User wants to skip the confirmation step | Honor it — but require an explicit "skip confirmation" or "just create it" from them. Default is to confirm. |
484	
485	## Common pitfalls
486	
487	| Pitfall | Why it bites | Fix |
488	| --- | --- | --- |
489	| Drafting before pre-flight checks | PR opened against stale base, with uncommitted work left behind | Run the pre-flight batch first |
490	| Not checking for an existing PR | Duplicate PR, or `gh pr create` errors out | Always `gh pr view` first |
491	| Pasting the Linear ticket verbatim | Description becomes a wall of duplicated text | Paraphrase the problem statement; link the rest |
492	| Filling all sections regardless of signal | Skim-defeating filler | Drop sections that don't carry meaning |
493	| Autopiloting `gh pr create` | Premature publication; harder to retract than to delay | Show draft, wait for confirmation |
494	| Inheriting the default 🤖 footer | Violates the repo's no-AI-attribution rule | Strip it from the body |
495	| Trusting a clean roborev as proof the code runs | Roborev reviews the diff, not test execution — a hardcoded test assertion (e.g. a literal YAML `if:` string) can still fail in CI | Run the mirrored test file / grep for affected literals before roborev (Step 5) |
496	| Using "WIP" in title instead of `--draft` | Title noise; doesn't actually mark the PR as draft | Use `gh pr create --draft` and a clean title |
497	| Linking to the PR's own branch name as "context" | The branch is implicit; this is noise | Only link to artifacts that aren't already obvious from the PR |
498	| Forgetting the linked GitHub issue entirely | Issue lingers open after merge with no trace back to the PR that fixed it | Resolve it in Step 2, `Closes #NNN` in Step 7, record disposition in Step 9, comment in Step 12b |
499	| Drafting `Closes #NNN` in Step 7 but the final body sent to `gh pr create` drops it (edits, re-drafts, template drift) | Issue never auto-closes even though Step 2/9 correctly flagged full resolution — happened for real on gtm-sdk#609/#628 | Step 12's mechanical grep gate on the literal `--body` string, not on what Step 7 intended to write |
500	
501	## Red flags (stop and rethink)
502	
503	- **About to `git push` without running `roborev review --wait` first.** This is the repository-wide roborev gate defined in the repo's agent instructions; no PR should skip it.
504	- **About to `git push` with more commits than the PR needs.** Squash to a coherent set first (Step 4); don't rely on GitHub's "Squash and merge" button to clean up history before review.
505	- Drafting a PR with no Linear ticket, no design artifact, and no conversation-derived motivation.
506	- Writing more than 3 paragraphs in Why. If you need that much, the work is probably two PRs.
507	- Including a `## Summary` section. This is the default template's tell — replace with `## Why`.
508	- Including a 🤖 footer.
509	- More than 5 bullets in any one section. Each bullet should be load-bearing.
510	- A title that ends in a period, or starts with "Update", "Fix some", "Misc", "Various".
511	- A title that uses a Conventional Commits prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). PR titles are formal sentences, not commit subjects.
512	- A title that describes *what* the diff does (e.g., "Add X helper", "Refactor Y module") when a *why* framing was available.
